stories.title: Object groups mutually bias each other’s perceived average size, as evidenced by neural and behavioural data
stories.description: The human visual system simultaneously computes summary statistics of object features, such as average size, across groups of objects. Evidence suggests that summary statistics across groups of objects (ensembles) are not independent but influence one another. We investigated whether an ensemble’s average size affects the perceived average size of another ensemble, and whether such changes are reflected in altered activation patterns in the visual cortex. Distractor ensembles’ average sizes altered the perceived average size of target ensembles in a contrast-like manner: Large distractor ensembles decreased the target ensembles’ perceived average sizes; conversely, smaller distractor ensembles increased target ensembles’ perceived average sizes. These contrast effects were reflected in more activated voxels in retinotopic regions when target ensembles were perceived as larger. Distractor ensembles’ voxel counts were similarly modulated by target ensembles’ average size, suggesting their perceived average size was also altered. Additionally, individual differences in the magnitude of the ensemble-size contrast effect covaried with activation in higher-level regions, including the left intraparietal sulcus (IPS) and middle temporal gyrus (MTG). Together, these findings suggest that ensemble summary statistics are contrasted, resulting in changes in perceived size and altered retinotopic activation pattern, with involvement of a network including left IPS and left MTG.

stories.title: Beyond the food tray: linking school nutrition and feeding programmes to student health and academic outcomes through health literacy and mental health
stories.description: School nutrition and feeding programmes are pivotal in addressing both public health and educational challenges, yet their multidimensional impacts remain underexplored in resource-constrained settings. Guided by the Health-Promoting Schools (HPS) framework, this study examined the relationships between s°chool nutrition and feeding programmes, students’ self-reported physical health, and academic performance, with health literacy and mental health as potential mediators. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among pupils in basic schools, comprising primary and junior high levels, using standardised questionnaires. Data were analysed with structural equation modelling (SEM). The findings indicate that feeding programmes are positively associated with students’ self-reported academic performance, with health literacy and mental health acting as indirect pathways. Health literacy was also found to mediate the relationship between feeding programmes and students’ perceived physical health. Effect size analysis suggested that these associations were stronger in disadvantaged communities. In conclusion, school feeding initiatives may function as dual-impact strategies linked to both health (SDG 3) and education (SDG 4). Policymakers are encouraged to integrate meal provision with health education to improve students’ well-being and learning experiences in resource-constrained contexts.

stories.title: Why You Shouldn’t Rush to Uninstall Your Genuine Licensed Copy
stories.description: The rapid advancement of AI coding technologies is fundamentally reshaping developers’ and tech industry practitioners’ perceptions of software development completion standards. Unlike the traditional coding paradigm that defines "degree of completion" solely by full manual implementation of all functional modules, AI-powered coding tools — including intelligent code generation assistants, automated bug detection systems, and AI-driven code optimization platforms — have redefined the benchmarks for measuring development maturity: a high-completion software product no longer requires 100% hand-coded lines, but emphasizes the seamless integration of AI-generated snippets, rigorous functional validation, robust performance output, and compliant maintainable architecture. This shift not only breaks the long-standing stereotype that equates "high completion" with massive manual coding workload, but also drives the global software development ecosystem to establish more efficient, AI-centric evaluation frameworks for development deliverables.
